::: {.callout-warning}
## Before you connect anything

- **Hot water and any hotplate stay in sight and within reach.** The stirred
  bath is **never left unattended** while it is heated, or while a
  mains-powered stirrer or hotplate is plugged in.
- Check the lead and the plug of the stirrer or hotplate before every
  session, keep the socket away from splashes, and switch off at the
  **mains** — not just at the vessel — before adjusting anything in or near
  the bath.
- Ice, a glass reference thermometer and wet hands are a slip-and-drop
  combination; keep the board and the rest of the electronics on a dry bench
  well clear of the bath.
- An analog input pin tolerates $0$ to $V_\mathrm{io}$ and nothing else — see
  [Before you connect anything](../S1-daq-static/handbook.qmd#sec-s1-hardware)
  in S1 for the same warning, which applies unchanged to both the divider and
  the in-amp output here.
:::

### 1. Build and verify the two front ends {#sec-t1-step-build}

```bash
arduino-io list
arduino-io info
```

Build the NTC's divider and the Pt1000's bridge plus instrumentation
amplifier, following [the conditioning board](../../hardware/conditioning-board.qmd)
for the amplifier stage. With the Pt1000 disconnected (open circuit) and
again with it shorted, confirm the bridge output sits where
@eq-t1-bridge predicts at the two extremes, before the sensor is ever put in
a bath. A discrepancy here is the bridge or the amplifier's own gain and
offset error, and it is one of the first components of the uncertainty budget
in @sec-t1-budget — measure it before you need it.

::: {.callout-tip}
## No rig yet?

The [reference data](index.qmd#sec-t1-index-data) models both front ends
numerically — the divider and the bridge, through the same S1 ADC model — so
every analysis task below runs against it unmodified. Build the hardware when
it is available and repeat the tasks with your own runs; nothing in the
templates changes.
:::

### 2. Build the ice bath {#sec-t1-step-ice}

Follow [the ice bath](../../hardware/thermal-rig.qmd#sec-therm-ice): crushed
ice, distilled water, packed to the bottom of the vessel, sensor and
reference thermometer both embedded in the slush well below the surface.
Give it a few minutes to settle before recording.

### 3. The six bath points {#sec-t1-step-points}

At each point — the ice bath, then five stirred-water temperatures spanning
your available range — with **both sensors already wired and in the bath**,
excited at their low (calibration) level:

1. Wait for the bath to reach a steady temperature and confirm it is well
   stirred, following [the check in the thermal rig
   page](../../hardware/thermal-rig.qmd#sec-therm-bath): move the reference
   thermometer to a few points in the bath and confirm they agree within its
   own resolution.
2. Read the reference thermometer and record it — this is the value that
   goes in **both** channels' `reference_value`, because both sensors are in
   the same bath at the same instant.
3. Record both channels together:

```bash
arduino-io mode 15 analog && arduino-io mode 16 analog
arduino-io stream 15,16 --hz 1000 --seconds 0.2 --csv data/cal-t50.csv
```

Name each file after its point (`cal-ice`, `cal-t20`, …), so the analysis
can find them without a lookup table, and spread the five stirred points
across as much of your bath's usable range as time allows — the fit in
@sec-t1-tasks is only as good as the range it was given.

::: {.callout-important}
## Re-measure the reference every time

Exactly as in [S1's calibration](../S1-daq-static/handbook.qmd#sec-s1-step-wire):
do not reuse a reference-thermometer reading from a previous point. A bath
that is still settling toward its target looks, in the data, exactly like a
sensor with an offset error, and there is no way to tell the two apart after
the fact.
:::

### 4. The self-heating run {#sec-t1-step-selfheat}

At **one** of the stirred-bath points already recorded — the shipped
reference data reuses the `t50` point — record one more file with both
sensors driven at their **high** excitation instead, everything else
unchanged: same bath, same wiring, same reference-thermometer reading.

```bash
arduino-io stream 15,16 --hz 1000 --seconds 0.2 --csv data/selfheat-high.csv
```

Record the excitation actually used (`channels[].excitation_v`, or the
bridge's `channels[].excitation_v` for the Pt1000) in both this sidecar and
the low-excitation point it is compared against — the shift between the two,
read through the fitted calibration curve, is what @sec-t1-tasks turns into
$\delta$.

### 5. Fill the sidecars {#sec-t1-step-sidecar}

Every run needs, beyond [S1's checklist](../S1-daq-static/handbook.qmd#sec-s1-step-sidecar):

- [ ] `channels[].quantity: temperature`, `channels[].unit: degC`
- [ ] `channels[].reference_value` and `.reference_u` — the reference
      thermometer's reading and its uncertainty, **the same value on both
      channels** at a given bath point
- [ ] `channels[].excitation_v` — the divider's $V_{cc}$ or the bridge's
      $V_\mathrm{exc}$ actually used for that run
- [ ] `channels[].conditioning.gain` and `.offset` — the Pt1000 in-amp's
      **fitted** gain and offset from step 1, not the design values
- [ ] `synthetic: false`

These are T1-specific extensions of the channel schema in
[Data format](../../data-format/index.qmd#sec-fields); the general fields
there are unchanged.
